cards.front: Define a mechanical wave, specifying its key requirements for propagation.
cards.back: A mechanical wave is a disturbance that propagates through a material medium by the oscillation of its particles, transferring energy without transferring matter. It absolutely requires a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to exist and propagate.

cards.front: How does the direction of particle oscillation compare to the direction of wave propagation for transverse versus longitudinal mechanical waves?
cards.back: In a transverse mechanical wave, particles of the medium oscillate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. In a longitudinal mechanical wave, particles of the medium oscillate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.

cards.front: Provide a common example of a transverse mechanical wave and explain why it fits this classification.
cards.back: Waves on a stretched string (e.g., a plucked guitar string) are transverse. When a segment of the string is displaced, the individual particles of the string oscillate up and down (perpendicular) while the wave itself propagates horizontally along the length of the string.

cards.front: Provide a common example of a longitudinal mechanical wave and explain why it fits this classification.
cards.back: Sound waves in air are longitudinal. As a sound wave propagates, air particles oscillate back and forth along the same direction as the wave's propagation, creating alternating regions of compression (higher pressure/density) and rarefaction (lower pressure/density).

cards.front: What physical quantities are typically oscillating or disturbed in a transverse wave versus a longitudinal wave?
cards.back: For a transverse wave, the disturbance is typically a displacement of particles perpendicular to the propagation direction (e.g., vertical displacement of a string). For a longitudinal wave, the disturbance involves displacement of particles parallel to the propagation direction, leading to oscillations in pressure and density (e.g., pressure fluctuations in a sound wave).

cards.front: Can a mechanical wave propagate through a perfect vacuum? Justify your answer.
cards.back: No. Mechanical waves require a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) for the oscillation of particles to transfer energy. A perfect vacuum lacks any particles, thus there is no medium to be disturbed or to transmit the wave's energy.

cards.front: State the formula for the wave speed ($v$) of a transverse wave on a stretched string, identifying the physical meaning of each variable.
cards.back: The wave speed ($v$) of a transverse wave on a stretched string is given by: $$v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}$$ where $T$ is the tension in the string (in Newtons) and $\mu$ is the linear mass density of the string (mass per unit length, in kg/m). This formula shows that wave speed increases with tension and decreases with linear mass density.
